text: Understanding databases is essential for managing information effectively. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases store data in tables with rows and columns, which makes the structure clear and organised. To get information from these tables, you use queries—special commands that search, filter, and sort data. Good data modelling helps you plan how tables connect before you build anything, which saves time later. Indexes are another useful tool: they work like a book's contents page, helping the database find data faster without scanning every row. NoSQL databases, on the other hand, are more flexible and suit unstructured or rapidly changing data. Choosing the right type depends on your project's needs.
